qs.q: External fertilization occurs in majority of
In the life cycle of mosses, the gametophyte has two stages (A and B). These stages can be called
qs.s: The predominant stage of the life cycle of a moss is the gametophyte, which consists of two stages. The first stage is protonema stage, which develops directly from a spore. The second stage is the leafy stage which develops from the secondary protonema as a lateral bud. They consist of upright slender axe bearing spirally arranged leaves. They are attached to the soil through multicellular and branched rhizoids. This stage bears the sex organs

qs.q: Number of meiosis for formation of 64 zygotes in angiosperm is 80 but in gymnosperms number of meiosis for formation of 64 zygotes will
qs.s: In both gymnosperms and angiosperms, the megaspore mother cell undergoes meiosis and produces four haploid megaspore. Out of four megaspore three will degenerate. Therefore, for formation of 64 zygotes in gymnosperm and angiosperm 64 meiosis in megaspore mother cell will required. Whereas the microspore mother cell in both gymnosperm and angiosperm undergoes meiosis and produced four haploid microspore. All the four will be functional therefore, for formation of 64 zygotes, 16 meiotic division in microspore mother cell will be required.

qs.q: In gymnosperm the microspores develop into a male gametophyte generation which
o: Is highly reduced and confined to only a limited number of cells
qs.s: In gymnosperm, microspores develop into a male gametophytic generation, which is highly reduced and is confined to only a limited number of cell. This reduced gametophyte is called a pollen grain. Its development takes place in microsporangia

qs.q: In a monoecious plant
o: Male and female sex organs are on different individuals
Male and female gametes are of two morphologically distinct types
Male and female sex organs are on the same individual
All the stamens are fused to form one unit
qs.s: A monoecious plant has both male and female reproductive organs on the same individual (plant) while dioecious plants are unisexual, having male and female reproductive organs on different individuals (plants).

qs.q: In which of the following, all listed genera belong to the same class of algae?
qs.s: Volvox, Spirogyra and Chlamydomonas are all green algae belonging to class-Chlorophyceae.

qs.q: Which of the following is incorrect with respect to angiosperms?
qs.s: Megaspores are haploid

qs.q: In Cycas stem, open vascular bundle is characterized by
o: Cambium present in between xylem and phloem
Xylem and phloem occurring on different radii
qs.s: In the stem of Cycas, the stele is eustele type, which consists of a ring of discrete vascular bundles. In these bundles, the primary cambium lies between the phloem and xylem.

qs.q: Which green alga shows heterotrichous habit and may have given rise to terrestrial (land) habit?
qs.s: Heterotrichous habit having prostrate and erect system by a filamentous thallus is must for evolution of terrestrial plants. It is found in green algae like Fritschiella, other examples are Draparnaldiopsis and Stigeocolonium.

qs.q:
The characteristic features of bryophytes are
I. main plant body is gametophytic
II. main plant body is sporophytic
III. requirement of water for fertilisation Which of the statements given above are correct?
qs.s: In bryophytes, the haploid gametophyte is dominant, long lived, green and independent whereas the diploid sporophyte is short lived and dependent upon the gametophyte. Water is essential for reproduction. The sex organs are multicellular and jacketed with sterile jacket

qs.q: Which is the tallest gymnospermic tree species?
qs.s: The gaint Sequoia is the world’s most massive tree and arguable the largest living organism on earth

qs.q: Anisogamous means both gamete are
qs.s: Fusion of morphologically dissimilar gametes, which may be motile or non-motile

qs.q: Usually plant body of brown algae is differentiated into
qs.s: The plant body of some highly advanced forms (e. g., Fucales, Laminariales) is differentiated into basal more or less root-like hold fast, erect branched or unbranched, tubular or compressed stipe and leaf-like blades the frond

qs.q: Ulothrix releases zoospore during
qs.s: In Ulothrix, the cells in the filament commonly produce and discharge the zoospores about the same time just after sunrise.

qs.q: The kidney-shaped covering of sorus in Dryopteris, is called
qs.s: Indusium is a protective kidney-shaped covering of sorus present in Dryopteris.

qs.q: Pollen grains in Pinus are
qs.s: Pollen grains in Pinus are monosaccate. In Pinus, pollen grain is unicellular, three layered: outer exine, the middle exo-intine and innermost intine.

qs.q: Characteristic of fern is
qs.s: The characteristic feature of fern’s leaves is circinate venation in which coiled arrangement of leaves and leaflets is found in the bud.

qs.q: Protonema is the stage in the life cycle of
qs.s: Protonema is the juvenile stage of moss resulting from the germinating meiospore and consists of a slender, green, branching system of filaments. In Funaria, the protonema stage is only vegetative and transitory, which precedes the upright, leafy gametophyte.

qs.q: Which of the following plant cells is not surrounded by a cell wall?
qs.s: Gamete is the haploid reproductive cell that fuses with another gamete to form a diploid zygote. These are not surrounded by the cell wall. On the other hand, root hair cell stem hair cell and bacterial cell, all possess a well defined cell wall.

qs.q: Top-shaped multiciliate male gametes and the mature seed, which bears only one embryo with two cotyledons, are characteristic features of
qs.s: Cycads possess top-shaped, multiciliate male gametes and he mature seed, which bears only one embryo with two cotyledons.

qs.q: Gametophytic and sporophytic phases are independent in
qs.s: The pteridophytes exhibit alternation of dominant sporophytic generation with an inconspicuous gametophytic generation. The sporophyte is differentiated into root, stem and leaves, while the small and inconspicuous gametophyte is independent and autotrophic.

qs.q: Which has vascular tissue, produces spores, but does not has seeds?
qs.s: Pteridophytes are vascular cryptogams. They generally produce spores but do not produce seeds. Bryophytes are non-vascular but spore forming cryptogams. Gymnosperms and angiosperms are vascular and seed forming phanerogams. All seed forming plants are also known as spermatophytes.

qs.q: Blue-green algae has
qs.s: c − phycocyanin pigment is found in blue-green algae (cyanobacteria).

qs.q: Which type of the rhizoids are present in Riccia?
qs.s: Unicellular smooth and tuberculated rhizoids are present in the region of midrib at ventral surface of Riccia.

qs.q: Identify the alga, which exhibits diplontic life cycle.
qs.s: Fucus, a brown alga displays a diploid life history. The zygote (2n) becomes an embryo and develops into the mature Fucus with receptacles at the tip of the algae.

qs.q: Gymnosperms are
qs.s: Gymnosperms are naked seeded plants because seeds are presents on the megasporophyll and are not enclosed with fruit wall due to lack of ovary wall

qs.q: Which of the following plant does not have Rhizobium containing root nodules?
qs.s: Pinus, is a gymnospermic plant that does not have Rhizobium containing root nodules.

qs.q: The diagram represents the life cycle of angiosperm. Choose the correct combination of labelling
o: A-Anther, B-Stigma, C-egg, D-Male gametophyte, E-ovule
A-Ovule, B-Stigma, C- Male gametophyte, D- Anther, E-Egg
A-Male gametophyte, B-Stigma, C-Anther, D-Egg, E-ovule
A-Stigma, B- Anther, C- Male gametophyte, D-Egg, E-ovule
qs.s: A- Stigma, B-Anther, C-Male gametophyte, D-Egg, E-Ovule

qs.q: Plants of this group are diploid and well adapted to extreme conditions. They grow bearing sporophylls in compact structures called cones. The group in reference is
qs.s: In gymnosperms the plants are diploid and well adapted to extreme conditions, e. g., the leaves in case of gymnosperms are well adopted to withstand extremes of temperature, humidity and wind. These shapes are xeromorphic adaptations because they reduce the amount of surface area available for evaporation. They grow bearing sporophylls incompact structures called cones

qs.q: After fertilisation the ovules develop into
qs.s: After fertilisation ovules develop into seeds and ovaries develop into fruit

qs.q: In comparition to pteridophyte, which one of the following algae exhibits diplontic life cycle?
qs.s: Most algal genera are haplontic, some of them such as Ectocarpus, Polysiphonia, Kelps are haplodiplontic. Fucus, on alga is diplontic

qs.q: Which one of the following plants functions as symbolic nitrogen-fixing plant?
qs.s: Azolla is an aquatic fen with bilobed leaves. It encloses large mucilage cavity, which contain filaments of Anabaena azollae. Anabaena fixes nitrogen from air into nitrogenous compounds, which accumulate in the air spaces in leaves and in return takes food material and shelter from plant.

qs.q: Which of the following is autotrophic?
qs.s: Nostoc is an alga. It contains chlorophyll and can prepare its own food, i. e., autotrophic.

qs.q: In some pteridophytes, sporophyll form distinct compact structures called...A... in...B... and...C... Here A, B and C refers to
qs.s: In some pteridophytes sporophylls may form distinct compact structure called cone or strobili. e. g., Selaginella, Equisetum

qs.q: Kelp (branched form) and Sargassam (filamentous form) belongs to
qs.s: Brown algae show great variation in size and form. They range from simple branched, filamentous forms (Ectocarpus) to profusely branched forms as represented by kelps, which may reach a height of 100 metres. The giant brown algae are called kelps. The largest kelps are Nereocystis (20-30 m) and Macrocystis (40-60 m)

qs.q: In Chlamydomonas, the meiosis occurs in
qs.s: In Chlamydomonas, the meiosis occurs in zygote.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements
I. The plants have magnificent property of retaining water. They can with hold water two hundred times more than their own weight. Hence, they are widely used by gardeners to keep cut plant parts moist during transportation and propagation
II. These plants grow as semiaquatic or submerged in acidic marshes. The older portions of plant die but do not decay due to peculiar germicidal properties The above statements belongs to which of the following bryophitic plant?
qs.s: Sphagnum

qs.q: First vascular plant is
qs.s: Pteridophytes are spore forming, non-seed bearing, non-flowering vascular plants. Thallophytes do not have vascular tissues. Bryophytes also come under thallophytes. Spermatophyte is a group of seed forming vascular plants. It includes gymnosperms and angiosperms.

qs.q: Female cone of Pinus is a
qs.s: The female cone of Pinus is formed by the aggregation of megasporophylls, which bear ovules. Each megasporophyll consists of a lower bract scale and a larger upper ovuliferous scale.

qs.q: Algae include unicellular forms like...A..., filamentous like...B... and colonical forms like...C.... Here A, B and C refer to
qs.s: Algae include unicellular forms like Chlamydomonas, filamentous like Ulothrix and colonial forms like Volvox

qs.q: The gametophyte of moss is
qs.s: Protonema is the juvenile stage of moss. It results from the germinating meiospore. When fully grown, it consists of a slender green, branching system of filaments called the protonema

Which of the following is not correctly matched?

qs.q: Male sex organs in an angiospermic flower is
qs.s: Male sex organ is stamen also known as androecium. It consists of an anther lobe and a filament. Anther produces pollen grains

qs.q: Which of the following is an algal parasite?
qs.s: Cephaleuros is a green parasitic alga, which causes red rust of tea and coffee.

qs.q: Mannitol is the stored food in
qs.s: Fucus belongs to class-Phaeophyceae, in which reserve food is found in form of laminarian, mannitol and oil.

qs.q: Select the correct sequential arrangement of reproductive structures for pteridophytes
o: Sporophyll → Strobilli → Sporangia → Spore mother cell → Spores
qs.s: Sporophyll → Strobili → Sporangia → Spore mother Cell → Spores

qs.q: In gymnosperms, the seeds are naked because they lack
qs.s: After fertilization, the ovary develops into fruit and ovary wall forms the fruit wall (pericarp). But gymnosperms have naked seeds because in gymnosperms, ovary (pericarp) is absent.

qs.q: The relationship between the alga Microcystis and the surrounding fauna corresponds to
qs.s: In ammensalism, one component (species) is harmed and the other remains unaffected. The alga Microcysis release hydroxyl amine that kills the surrounding fauna but the alga itself remain unaffected.

qs.q: Bryophytes resemble algae in the following aspect.
o: Filamentous body, presence of vascular tissues and autotrophic nutrition
Differentiation of plant body into root, stem and leaves and autotrophic nutrition
Thallus like plant body, presence of roots and autotrophic nutrition
Thallus like plant body, lack of vascular tissues and autotrophic nutrition
qs.s: Bryophytes resemble algae in many ways, some of which are (i) thalloid plant body (ii) absence of roots (iii) absence of complex vascular tissues (iv) autotrophic mode of nutrition (v) reserve food material is true starch.

qs.q: Algae are also found in association with
qs.s: Algae are chlorophyll-bearing, simple thalloid, autotrophic and largely aquatic organisms. They occur in a variety of other habitats: moist stones, soil and wood. Some of them also occur in association with fungi (lichen) and animals (e. g., on sloth bear)

qs.q: The bryophytes are divided into
qs.s: The bryophytes are divided into liverworts and mosses

qs.q:
Consider the following statements
I. In red algae vegetative reproduction takes place by fragmentation
II. In red algae the food is stored as floridean starch, which is very similar to amylopectin and glycogen is structure
III. Cell wall of red algae consists of chitin Which of the statements given above are correct?
qs.s: In red algae vegetative reproduction takes place by fragmentation. The reserve food material is in the form of floridean starch. It is very much similar to amylopectin and glycogen in structure. The cell wall is made up of cellulose, pectic compounds and certain mucopolysaccharides called phycocolloids

qs.q: In Selaginella, trabeculae are the modification of
qs.s: The stem of Selaginella, Kraussiana shows distelic condition. Some air spaces develop between the endodermal cells isolating two steles from the cortex. The endodermal cells elongate to form trabeculae connecting the two tissues. The stele remains suspended by this unicelled (rarely multicelled) trabeculae.

qs.q: Which one of the following formed in Spirogyra is different based on its nucleus?
qs.s: The akinetes and aplanospores are asexual bodies in Spirogyra. These are haploid structures. The zygospore is formed during sexual reproduction by fusion of two protoplasts. Prior to germination, the diploid zygospore nucleus undergoes meiosis.

qs.q: During development of embryo in archegonium of Bryophyta, its posterior part form protective embryo cover, which is called
qs.s: The archegonial venter forms a protective covering around the embryo called calyptra.

qs.q: Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria, Sargassum and Fucus belongs to the class
qs.s: Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria, Sargassum and Fucus, all are the examples of class-Phaeophyceae

qs.q: Sexual reproduction in Spirogyra is an advanced feature because it shows
o: Different sizes of motile sex organs
Same size of motile sex organs
qs.s: In Spirogyra, the sexual reproduction involves the fusion of two morphologically identical isogametes, and physiologically dissimilar anisogametes. This is an advanced feature. In this, the active gamete is known as the male and the passive as the female.

qs.q: Buxbaumia aphylla is a classical example of
qs.s: Boxboumia aphylla is a classical example of saprophytic bryophyte

qs.q: Identify the given figures of algae and select the correct option
qs.s: A-Fucus, B-Polysiphonia, C-Porphyra, D-Dictyota

qs.q: Mosses and ferns are found in moist and shady places because both
o: Require presence of water for fertilization
Do not need sunlight for photosynthesis
Depend for their nutrition on microorganisms, which can survive only at low temperature

qs.q: Elater mechanism or spore dispersal is exhibited by
qs.s: The diploid bispiral elaters are hygroscopic. They help in the dispersal of spores in Marchantia.

qs.q: Which of the following can be regarded as seedless vascular plants?
qs.s: Pteridophytes are called vascular cryptogams also known as seedless vascular plants. They produce spores rather than seeds

qs.q: Fern gametophyte shows...... nature.
qs.s: Fern gametophyte is homothallic. It bears male gamete (antherozoid) and the female gemete (egg, cell).

qs.q: The peculiar feature of Marchantia palmata is
qs.s: An androgynous receptacle is the one which contains antheridia on upper side and archegonia on lower side, e. g., Marchantia.

qs.q: Chlorophyll- a, chlorophyll- d and phycoerythrin are characteristics of class
qs.s: Class-Rhodophyceae. In class-Rhodophyceae the photosynthetic pigments located in the chromatophores are chlorophyll-a, d, α - β -carotene, xanthophylls and biliprotein (r-phycoerythrin) (red in colour) and r -phycocyanin (blue in colour)

qs.q: Ramenta is the characteristic of
qs.s: In Dryopteris, the young parts of the leaves and rhizome while in Cycas, scaly leaves remain covered with small brown hair called ramenta.

qs.q: Sperm of Cycas is
qs.s: The sperm of Cycas is top-shaped with numerous cilia arising from a spiral line running from the pointed end towards the broader end. The sperm of Cycas is perhaps the largest of all known male cell in plant and animal kingdom.

qs.q: Archegoniophore is present in
qs.s: IN Marchantia a bryophyte, the archegonia (female sex organ) are borne on special branches called archegoniophore or female receptacles. Each archegoniophore has rows of archegonia protected by involucre or perichaetium.

qs.q: In Pinus, male cone bears a large number of
qs.s: In Pinus, each male cone consists of an elongated axis, bearing a number of spirally arranged microsporophylls. On the underside of which two microsporangia develop and get filled with microspores (pollen grains).

qs.q: Which one pair of examples will correctly represent the grouping spermatophyta according to one of the schemes of classifying plants?
qs.s: Ginkgo is a gymnospermic plant, so it comes before angiospermic plant, Pisum (pea).

qs.q:
Read carefully the following statements about pteridophytes
I. They are called vascular cryptogams
II. They produce spores rather than seeds
IIII. They are used for medicinal purposes
IV. They are used as soil binders
V. They are frequently grown as ornaments Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: I, II, III, IV and V
qs.s: Pteridophytes are spore forming non-seed bearing, non-flowering vascular plants. An anthimintic drug is obtained from the rhizomes and petioles of the fern. Dryopteris, Lycopodium is used in treatment of rheumatism and disorders of lungs and kidneys. They are used as soil binders. Presence of heterospory (morphologicacally two levels of spores) is a characteristic features of pteridophytes

qs.q: Coralloid roots are found in
qs.s: Coralloid root is developed in Cycas. It contain an algae zone in the cortex. This algal zone contains blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) like Nostoc, Anabaena, which grow in symbiotic association with coralloid root

qs.q: Leaf in young condition in fern is called
qs.s: Leaf in young condition in fern is called circinate ptyxis (i. e., coiled like a spring).
